newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices rise ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices rise ahead of weekend.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were mostly higher Friday amid cooler weather in parts of the Midwest and firmer futures, market sources said.

On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, swing prices on Transco (Station 65) were steady to higher at $1.87-1.90, while Henry Hub gained a few cents to $1.89-1.93 per mmBtu. Most other Gulf prices were also higher in the mid-to-high $1.80s.
At 1411 EST, NYMEX's Henry Hub May natgas futures were 3.5 cents firmer at $1.94, the high of the session.
In south Texas, prices were up only about one cent to the low-$1.80s, as cooler, rainy weather in the region capped air-conditioning demand.
At the New York city-gate, the market extended its losses ahead of a mild weekend, as prices drifted another two to five cents lower to $2.08-2.13.
In the Appalachian region, prices were steady to higher at $2.02-2.05 on Columbia and $2.12-2.13 on CNG in response to the inflated values on the Gulf pipes.

In the Midcontinent, prices were up about two cents to about $1.75-1.76 as cooler weather moved into the area. Forecasts are calling for mostly below-normal temperatures to continue through at least the middle of next week.

Despite the strengthening in the Gulf, Permian basin prices eased by about two cents due to the expected return of Pacific Gas and Electric's 1,073 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear unit in California.
The company said the unit will likely restart sometime today and achieve full power this weekend.
At the southern California border, prices also reacted to the plant restart by falling three cents to $1.79-1.81.
